speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; please describe exactly when it started and if you recall any recent insect bites, injuries, or changes in your immune system. To help narrow this down, would you mind telling me if you have any underlying conditions like diabetes or are currently taking any immunosuppressive medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Thank you for the details; the history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, recent corticosteroid use for uveitis, and an ant bite at the site of a rapidly enlarging, painful ulcer strongly suggests this inflammatory condition rather than a simple infection. Given your immunosuppressed state and systemic diseases, we must rule out cellulitis or vasculitis; would you like me to order a wound culture, CBC, and ESR, and should I request images of the lesion to assess its borders and depth?
